text:
maria: heads up — we're proposing a new client flag `runtime_policy=server` that makes SDKs defer routing decisions to the control plane. thinking through compat and console telemetry. thoughts?
aj: fwiw this will change effective quota and latency profiles for some customers, so we need console visibility before wide rollout.
ryan: can we avoid a hard-break default? opt-in seems safer. default "opt-out" today.
sophie: +1 to opt-in. but we should offer a migration header so customers can test: `X-Redwood-Routing: runtime=server`
kevin: what does server routing actually change? clarify for SDK folks: is it just header propagation or handshake?
maria: both — SDK will stop picking route variants, and will attach route hint metadata + a new handshake to fetch policy token. sample header:```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Redwood-Routing: runtime=server;policy-v=1
```
aj: need to list exact telemetry events for console: policy_decision, fallback, latency_breakdown, quota_bucket_hit. console needs per-request tag to filter.
sophie: agree. also we should emit a sampling flag so telemetry doesn't explode. maybe `policy_sampling=1/100` per org.
infra-bot: note: deploying control plane change will require schema bump for `/route` response (adds `policy_id`, `quota_group`). CI will fail if clients expect old shape.
kevin: then SDKs must tolerate extra keys. implement lenient parsing and log a debug message when unknown keys present.
ryan: about rollout — propose three-stage: (1) feature flag on control plane + SDK support behind experimental flag; (2) opt-in beta customers + console telemetry tile; (3) flip default to server for new SDK releases after 8 weeks.
maria: +1. add deprecation notice in client changelog and communication to customers with large quotas.
aj: we also need a preview dashboard in Console -> Routing -> "Policy decisions". UX ask: quick filter by model, region, and policy_id.
sophie: can console show sampled request traces linking to trace IDs? that's incredibly helpful for debugging fallbacks.
kevin: implement small telemetry contract: `policy_decision` event with fields: `policy_id`, `decision`, `latency_ms`, `quota_bucket`. payloads must be base64 JSON string to avoid schema churn.
ryan: base64 feels hacky. prefer versioned JSON payloads and a `schema_version` field. we can support optional base64 later.
kevin: ok will change to `schema_version` and version=1.
maria: QA plan: create a dedicated test org with heavy synthetic load hitting both SDK vX (client-side routing) and vX+1 (server routing). measure latencies, P50/P95, and quota attribution.
aj: also ensure logs capture missing handshake tokens — common customer pitfall. add clear error messages: "policy token required for server routing; enable runtime_policy or include X-Redwood-Routing header"
sophie: docs: add migration guide with example code for Py/TS/Go. quick example for py:```python
# opt into server routing
from redwood import Client
client = Client(runtime_policy='server')
res = client.generate('...')
```
kevin: timeline: I'll land SDK opt-in switches in the go/py/ts repos this week behind feature flags. infra will add telemetry events to staging control plane.
infra-bot: reminder: add feature flag `runtime_policy.server.enable` to release config and gate rollout.
ryan: can we make a small compatibility shim so older SDKs that don't understand `policy_v` still work? fallback to default client-side routing.
maria: yes, control plane will fallback if SDK handshake missing. but add warning logs and dashboard rows for "legacy-clients".
aj: final ask — communicate this to Solutions & Support with a short checklist: how to detect, how to toggle back to client routing, and known performance tradeoffs.
kevin: I'll draft the checklist and put on /doc repo; will ping you all for review.
sophie: thanks — let's sync Thursday 10am PT for rollout gating call. :calendar:
